newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - Oct 24.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- President Fidel Ramos stops the demolition of squatter shanties after holding a dialogue with urban poor representatives and Church leaders (ALL PAPERS)
- President Fidel Ramos rejects a proposal by Nobel peace prize winner Jose Ramos-Horta that he brokers peace talks between East Timor and Indonesia (ALL PAPERS)

- Four mining firms and 14 other companies are being investigated for their possible involvement in a fishkill that left about 30 tonnes of dead fish in Manila Bay last October, the environment department says (PHLIPPINE STAR)
- One of the leaders of the rightist soliders who staged the December 1989 coup attempt has been reinstated as officer of the Army (MANILA STANDARD)
- Senators have agreed to reconsider a plan to open the retail trade to foreign competition. (BUSINESSWORLD)

- The International Finance Corp pledges to pour in $250 million in fresh investment into the Philippines next year, focusing on new areas of private infrastructure and emerging sectors. (BUSINESS DAILY)
- The U.S. government is protesting a plan of the Philippine Tariff Commission to increase the tariff on certain chocolate products. (PHILIPPINE DAILY INQUIRER)
